title: Your Busy Heart
blurb: It is as big as your fist and it never takes a day off. Meet the pump that keeps you alive.

chapters.title: A Pump the Size of a Fist
chapters.text:
Put your hand on the left side of your chest. Can you feel a gentle thump, thump, thump? That is your heart at work.

The heart is a strong muscle. It is about the size of your own fist. Its job is to pump blood around your body. Blood carries oxygen and food to every part of you, from your brain to your toes.

Unlike the muscles in your arms, your heart never rests. It starts beating before you are born, and it keeps going every second of your life, day and night.

You can try to stop your breath for a moment, but you can never tell your heart to stop. It works by itself, so you can think about other things.

chapters.title: Four Rooms
chapters.text:
Inside, your heart has four spaces called chambers. You can think of them as four little rooms. The two upper chambers are called atria, and the two lower ones are called ventricles.

A wall in the middle divides the heart into a left side and a right side. The right side receives blood that has travelled around your body and sends it to the lungs to pick up fresh oxygen. The left side receives the fresh blood from the lungs and pumps it out to the rest of the body.

Small doors called valves open and close between the chambers. They make sure that the blood flows in only one direction. Every thump you feel is the sound of the valves closing.

chapters.title: Roads for Blood
chapters.text:
Blood does not float around freely. It travels inside tubes called blood vessels. If you stretched all your blood vessels in one line, they would be many thousands of kilometres long.

There are three main kinds. Arteries carry blood away from the heart. They have thick, strong walls because the blood inside them is under pressure. Veins carry blood back to the heart. Capillaries are the thinnest vessels, thinner than a hair. They link arteries and veins and pass oxygen to the cells.

It takes about one minute for a drop of blood to travel all the way around your body and return to your heart.

chapters.title: Feel Your Pulse
chapters.text:
Every time the heart squeezes, it pushes blood into the arteries and makes them stretch a little. You can feel this stretch as a pulse. The easiest places are your wrist and your neck.

To measure your pulse, place two fingers on the inside of your wrist, below your thumb. Do not use your thumb itself, because it has a pulse of its own. Count the beats for fifteen seconds and multiply by four. This gives your heart rate for one minute.

When you are resting, a child's heart usually beats about seventy to one hundred times a minute. When you run or jump, your muscles need more oxygen, so the heart beats faster.

chapters.title: A Happy Heart
chapters.text:
You can look after your heart every day. The first rule is to move. Running, swimming, cycling and playing football make your heart stronger, just as lifting heavy things makes your arms stronger. Doctors say children should be active for about an hour every day.

The second rule is to eat well. Fruit, vegetables, fish, nuts and whole grains keep the vessels healthy. Too much sugar and too much oil are not good for them.

The third rule is to sleep. While you rest, your heart slows down and your body can repair itself.

Finally, never smoke, and keep away from smoke. It harms the heart and the lungs. If you follow these rules, your busy heart will work hard for you for a very long time.
